Here's your low-pressure sketch reference pack — all three items are open in tabs for you right now.

📌 1) FIGURE REFERENCE (Pinterest pin)
"Body Drawing Base: Human Figure References & Guide"
https://uk.pinterest.com/pin/body-drawing-base-human-figure-references-guide--315674255148612403/
Why it works for a beginner: it's a body-drawing base/guide that shows proportions, gesture, and poses before you add clothing or detail — exactly the "clear and useful" foundation you want for basic figure practice. (Note: Pinterest shows a login prompt, but the pin image and description load fine without signing in.)

🏚️ 2) 1500s ENGLISH HUT (background setting)
A believable simple one-room wooden hut/cabin with a thatched roof, found via a Bing Images search for "1500s english one room wooden hut medieval cottage."
Direct image link: https://i.pinimg.com/736x/6f/33/72/6f3372e50bd6dd71bdda08b8d6e120f3.jpg
Source search page (open in your browser): https://www.bing.com/images/search?q=1500s+english+one+room+wooden+hut+medieval+cottage
It's a simple, rustic, single-room structure — easy to reduce to a few lines as a background.

😾 3) ANGRY CAT MOOD REFERENCE (Bored Panda)
Exact page title: "40 Times People Just Had To Snap A Pic Of Their Angry, But Cute Cats | Bored Panda"
https://www.boredpanda.com/cute-angry-cats/
Full of exaggerated-but-lovable angry expressions (squinted eyes, flattened "airplane" ears, bared teeth) — perfect for a fun character expression study.

💡 How they could work together in one simple sketch:
Draw a single cozy scene: the small thatched one-room hut as the backdrop (just a box, a slanted roof, a door, and a puff of smoke). In front of it, place one simple figure in a basic standing or seated pose using the body-base reference — keep it loose, no fine detail. Give that figure an "angry cat" face: flattened ears, narrowed eyes, a little scowl. The humor comes from the mismatch — a grumpy little character huffing in front of their tiny 1500s hut, like they're mad about the drafty thatch or a cold soup. It's a low-pressure way to practice a figure, a simple environment, and a big expressive face all in one relaxed sketch.

All three tabs (Pinterest pin, Bing hut image, and the Bored Panda page) are left open for you.
